business.description: Three jobs a small model on your own computer does: news mentions of a business, private bookkeeping categorisation and equipment lot manifests.

sections.headline: A model on your own computer, *doing paid work.*
sections.lede: Three jobs a small model can do well when it is asked a narrow question and checked against what the text already says. Each runs on one computer, keeps a receipt for every answer, and sends nothing to an outside service.

items.title: Mentions of a business
items.text: What the news sources this installation reads said about a business, with namesakes set aside and the items that need doing something about listed first.

items.title: Books on your own machine
items.text: Bank and card lines booked to a client's accounts, learning from earlier months, with the unsure lines held for review.

items.title: Lot manifests
items.text: A seller's photos and listing turned into a manifest a buyer can price, with every gap listed for the seller to fill.

items.title: The text settles what it can
items.text: Names, model numbers, counts and stated conditions are copied as written. Rules decide what the words make certain, such as toner holding no data.

items.title: The model answers a narrow question
items.text: Is this the business or a namesake. Which of these accounts. What kind of equipment. Every answer keeps its probabilities and the exact model file that gave it.

items.title: Unsure answers go to a person
items.text: A low-confidence answer is held for review, and anything the seller or source did not state is listed to confirm.

sections.headline: What the news said about a business, *namesakes set aside.*
sections.lede: bonfyre monitor reads the items an installation already collects, keeps the ones about the business, and lists first the few that call for a reply, carry a risk or offer an opening. This page shows a real run over 30 days of archived headlines naming Apple.

sections.headline: Bank lines booked to your accounts, *on your own computer.*
sections.lede: bonfyre books learns from the lines a client has already categorised and books a new month from that. The lines it is unsure of go to a local model, which sees how similar lines were booked before. Transactions never leave the computer.

sections.headline: A seller's photos and listing, *turned into a manifest.*
sections.lede: bonfyre manifest reads lot photos and listings on one computer, copies the make, model, part number and count exactly as written, and asks a local model what each unit is and whether it holds data to wipe. Anything the seller did not state is listed to confirm. The output loads into the ITAD acquisition desk.
